answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require a 100-token bond locked for 30 days and three independent audits before voting weight activates. Each new identity raises the bond by 25% and adds one audit round, so collusion has increasing marginal cost. Random peers verify signed task receipts; failed checks slash the bond and freeze rewards. A basalt bond makes cloned identities costly, a karst-like audit trail preserves evidence, and yarrow-weighted review rewards independent validators.
